answer.answer:
Six things stand upstream of robotic assembly, and only one of them is a machine: the robotic arm itself. The other five are ways of preparing the work: a path plan, components made highly standardised, prefabrication off site, a delivery and business model that can carry the robot, and, at one remove, the enclosed factory condition. Path-planning in turn needs sensing and point-cloud geometry before it can run, and the wider automated workflow rests on workforce training, which is the requirement most often present in the record. Weights are very uneven: standardisation and path-planning are drawn on by about half the coded cases, while the mobile factory appears in one case only and its link to assembly is asserted in the literature and carried by none of the fifty.

**What robotic assembly requires**

PR4 "Robotic assembly" carries four inbound and six outbound dependency edges, and the complete set is in front of me, so the following is exact. 13 of the 50 coded cases draw on PR4 itself. [1] Its requirements are:

- The machine. RE2 "Robotic arm" enablesCapability PR4, carried by 12 of the 50 coded cases [1], with the converse stated too: PR4 dependsOn RE2, carried by 12 of the 50 [1]. 22 of the 50 coded cases draw on RE2. [1] This is the only Resource among the six.
- The plan. PR12 "Path-planning" enablesCapability PR4, on peer-reviewed evidence, carried by 2 of the 50 coded cases [1], although 26 of the 50 draw on path-planning in its own right [1].
- The parts. AT7 "Highly standardised" enablesCapability PR4, carried by 10 of the 50, on the finding that Japanese automated erection systems rely on standardised prefabricated components [1]; 25 of the 50 draw on AT7 [1]. Related but separate: PR4 hasPrecondition PR2 "Prefabrication/off-site", carried by 4 of the 50 [1], with 20 of the 50 drawing on PR2 [1].
- The organisation. PR4 dependsOn RI12 "Delivery/business model/work culture", carried by 2 of the 50 [1]; 16 of the 50 draw on RI12 [1].
- The enclosure. CO12 "Mobile factory" enablesCapability PR4, carried by 0 of the 50 coded cases [1], and only 1 of the 50 draws on CO12 at all [1]. This is a Condition, not a machine, and the edge is cited in the literature and carried by none of the 50.

**What path-planning itself needs**

PR12 hasPrecondition RE4 "3D scanner/sensor/camera/ICT", carried by 22 of the 50, on the ground that onboard localisation is a fundamental prerequisite for autonomous operation [1]; 39 of the 50 draw on RE4 [1]. PR12 dependsOn CO16 "3D point-cloud", carried by 9 of the 50. [1] Two computational routes feed it: RE1 "Parametric/computational/data-driven algorithm/machine code" enablesCapability PR12, carried by 7 of the 50 [1], and RE8 "Machine Learning/AI algorithm" enablesCapability PR12, carried by 5 of the 50 [1]. Against this, RI5 "Location dependent/site constraint" constrains PR12, carried by 15 of the 50, because reliable GNSS is typically unavailable indoors [1].

**The wider workflow**

Reading "build" to include the whole production chain, 44 of the 50 coded cases draw on AR9 "Automated production workflow" [1]. RE9 "Project management system" enablesCapability AR9, carried by 26 of the 50 [1], CO3 "BIM-based environment" enablesCapability AR9, carried by 8 [1], and RE13 "IFC" enablesCapability AR9, carried by 1 [1]. The heaviest condition is human: AR9 dependsOn RI6 "Require workforce training", carried by 38 of the 50, because the sophistication of digital technologies prohibits adoption by less technologically familiar workers [1]. The same holds where people work alongside the machine: CO6 "Human-robot interaction" dependsOn RI6, carried by 27 of the 50 [1], and CO6 dependsOn RI18 "Regulatory/legal concern" on standards evidence, carried by 2 of the 50, while CO6 mitigates RI20 "Work safety concern", carried by 4 [1].

**What it yields**

PR4 amplifies VA2 "Reduce time/improve productivity/efficiency", carried by 13 of the 50 [1], PR4 amplifies VA6 "Reduce cost", carried by 7 [1], and PR4 enablesCapability VA10 "Reduce errors/constraints", carried by 1 [1]. More broadly, AR9 enablesCapability VA1 "Reduce human dependency", carried by 42 of the 50 [1], and AT3 "Bespoke DFAB technology" amplifies VA2, carried by 35 of the 50 [1].

**Deployed record**

Three deployed processes in the context all perform assembly and all sit at technology readiness level 9: census_RXH1-1, adopted to address integration, performing assembly, steelwork and welding on the structural core, building envelope, facade or curtain wall [2], from Firm_013; census_RXH4-1, adopted to address cost and labor, performing assembly and concrete work on the structural core, building envelope, facade or curtain wall [3], from Firm_166; and census_RXH7-2, adopted to address quality, safety, labor and market, performing assembly and tiling on the building envelope, facade or curtain wall [4], from Firm_125 and the census record of process RP29. These records confirm that robotic assembly is in service at full readiness on steel, concrete and facade work, but the context does not link any of them to the individual enablers above, so I cannot say which of the six requirements each one exhibits.
